## 2. Privacy Policy

### Who We Are
[Product Name] is operated by [Operator Legal Name], based in [Country/State of Operation]. For privacy questions, contact [Support Contact Email].

### What the Service Does
[Product Name] is a business tool for managing distribution sales — order invoicing, distributor ledger tracking, and sales reporting — used internally by an operator's team.

### Information We Collect
- **Account information:** name, email address, and a securely hashed password (via bcrypt — the actual password is never stored) for each user account.
- **Business data you enter:** distributor names and contact details, product/manufacturer catalogs, order and invoice records, ledger/payment history, and any notes added to orders.
- **Technical/security data:** basic request logs (timestamps, IP address, requested endpoint) generated by standard web server logging, used only for operating and securing the Service — not for tracking or profiling individuals.
- **We do not collect:** payment card details (no payment processor is integrated), or any data through advertising or analytics trackers (none are used).

### How We Use Information
Solely to operate the Service: authenticating users, enforcing role-based access, generating invoices/reports, maintaining the ledger, and securing the app (e.g. rate-limiting, audit logging of who changed what). We do not sell data, use it for advertising, or share it with third parties except as described below.

### Cookies
The Service uses exactly two cookies, both strictly necessary for the app to function — no analytics or advertising cookies. See the separate **Cookie Policy** for full detail.

### Third-Party Services
**Google Drive (optional backup feature only):** if an admin chooses to back up data, exported files are uploaded directly from that admin's browser to their own Google Drive account, using a Google sign-in the admin must complete every time (nothing is cached or stored). This app's server never receives, sees, or stores the admin's Google credentials or Drive contents — the connection is browser-to-Google directly. The permission requested (`drive.file`) is Google's narrowest scope: it only allows the app to manage files it creates itself, not to read anything else already in that Drive. See `SECURITY.md` section 7 for full technical detail. No other third-party services are integrated into this app.

### Data Retention
Business data (orders, ledger entries, distributor/product records) is retained for as long as [Operator Legal Name] operates the Service, since it constitutes the business's own operating records. Account data for a deactivated user is retained per [Operator Legal Name]'s internal record-keeping needs; contact [Support Contact Email] with deletion requests.

### Your Rights
Depending on where you're located, you may have rights to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal account information (this does not extend to business records like orders/ledger entries, which belong to the operating business, not to an individual user). **If you have users in the EU/UK or California**, additional rights under GDPR or CCPA respectively may apply — [Operator Legal Name] should confirm and document specific compliance steps for those jurisdictions before serving users there; this generated draft does not itself constitute that compliance work.

### International Data Transfers
[State here whether your hosting/database infrastructure is in a different country than your users, and if so, note the transfer mechanism you rely on — this depends on where you actually deploy the app and needs to be filled in once that's decided.]

### Children's Privacy
The Service is a business tool not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect data from children under 13 (or the relevant age of consent in your jurisdiction).

### Security
Account passwords are hashed (never stored as plain text); sessions use httpOnly, CSRF-protected cookies; role-based access is enforced on every request; failed-login lockout and rate limiting protect against brute-force attempts. Full technical detail is documented in this project's `SECURITY.md`. No security measure is perfect — no warranty of absolute security is made.

### Changes to This Policy
Material changes will be communicated via the app or by email to admin accounts, with an updated effective date.

## 3. Cookie Policy

### What Cookies Are
Cookies are small text files a website stores in your browser, used to remember information between visits or requests.

### Cookies This App Uses

| Cookie | Type | Purpose | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsl_session` | Strictly necessary | Keeps you signed in; stores your session token. Set as `httpOnly` — not readable by any JavaScript, including this app's own frontend code. | 8 hours, or until logout |
| `csrf_token` | Strictly necessary | Security token used to confirm requests actually came from this app's own frontend, preventing cross-site request forgery. Not `httpOnly` — the app's frontend JavaScript needs to read it to send it back on each request. | Session-length |

**That's the complete list.** This app does not use analytics cookies (no Google Analytics or similar), advertising/tracking cookies, or any third-party cookies of its own.

### Third-Party Cookies
The only third-party involved at all is **Google**, and only during the optional Drive backup flow: while the Google sign-in popup is open, Google may set its own cookies in that popup window, governed entirely by [Google's cookie policy](https://policies.google.com/technologies/cookies) — this app has no visibility into or control over those. They are not set by, or on behalf of, this app.

### Managing Cookies
Because both of this app's cookies are strictly necessary for login to function, disabling them will prevent you from staying signed in. If you want to clear them, use your browser's standard cookie management (usually under Settings → Privacy) and search for this app's domain.

### A Note on Cookie Consent Banners
Since this app uses only strictly-necessary cookies (no analytics, no advertising, no tracking), a cookie-consent banner is generally *not* legally required under EU/UK ePrivacy rules, which specifically exempt cookies "strictly necessary" for a service the user requested (like staying logged in). **This is a general rule, not a confirmed legal conclusion for your specific situation** — confirm this with a lawyer if you're serving EU/UK users, and revisit it immediately if you ever add analytics or advertising cookies, since that would change the answer.

### Changes to This Policy
Material changes will be communicated the same way as changes to the Privacy Policy.
